conjecture: Migration length ell(M), the number of hexagon rotations in Purbhoo's migration (arXiv:0705.1184) of a mosaic to its Littlewood-Richardson tableau, is a non-trivial q-grading on c^lambda_{mu nu}.

tree.approach: ell(M) = #migration steps is a non-trivial statistic on the fibre over (lambda,mu,nu), so that G(q) = sum_M q^{ell(M)} refines the LR coefficient
tree.reason: REFUTED. ell admits an exact potential: the height phi(a,b,c,e)=b+e on the Z^4 lift of a mosaic increases by exactly 1 at every migration step, so ell(M) = sum_{destination cells} phi - sum_{source cells} phi depends only on the boundary data. G(q) = c^lambda_{mu nu} q^{ell_0} is a monomial. Verified: 361 fibres, 1 distinct value of ell each; 21 fibres with multiplicity >= 2 (Gr(3,6), Gr(3,7), Gr(4,7)), all constant; closed form for ell_0 agrees on all 361 fibres and all 487 journeys.

children.reason: No such statistic exists. The word 'length' occurs in the paper only as 'side length'; there is no step count, q-analogue or grading anywhere in it. ell(M) is my construction, attributed to Purbhoo across four journals in error. children.approach: (T1) as carried for four cycles: migration is a rewriting system; prove it confluent with constant path length via a local diamond lemma built on the Wake Crossing Lemma
children.reason: Ill-posed. Migration is a deterministic algorithm (section 3.1): the rhombus order is the standard order of the flock's tableau and is total; the minimal hexagon is asserted unique; the 120-degree rotation is disambiguated. There is no nondeterminism, so there is nothing to be confluent. The Wake Crossing Lemma is what makes the map order-preserving (Theorem 1), not what makes a rewriting system confluent.

Purbhoo's literal 3-fold tie-break ('some edge ends up exactly horizontal or vertical') cannot select the forward rotation in any fixed frame; and the 'unique minimal hexagon' is not unique (1593 of 13541 steps had several). Rule reconstructed from his own section 4 (the wake is a path, so no position repeats) plus forward motion, with the h/v condition as tie-break.
(T1) reposed well: does ell depend on the order in which the rhombi of the flock are migrated? Enumerate all admissible orders per mosaic.

phi(a,b,c,e) = b+e is a height on the Z^4 lift with Delta phi = 1 at every migration step; hence ell is a potential difference and depends only on the boundary. phi does not factor through the plane projection.

Exhaustive classification: 90 hexagon regions up to translation, every tiling, every rhombus, every rotation. Under Purbhoo's constraints (hexagon weakly right of the rhombus's leftmost point; exactly one rhombus in the hexagon; Proposition 3.1's two admissible orientations) all weakly-forward steps have Delta phi = 1 except one configuration.

GAP: the strictly vertical 180-degree step exists in two directions. SHARPENED 2026-10-06 c1: the two directions are one geometric picture read two ways (the hexagon is R (+) [0,1]u_60, the rhombus swept one unit perpendicular to travel), hence mutually inverse, hence NO potential can assign +1 to both -- the gap is irreducible and can only be closed by a reachability argument. Hexagon minimality cannot discriminate (all 15 admissible local moves use 4-tile hexagons). Reduced to two named hypotheses (G) and (G2).

The strictly vertical step is a unit translation of the travelling rhombus by +-u_60, perpendicular to the travel direction u_150; the hexagon is the Minkowski sum R (+) [0,1]u_60, a 4-tile zonogon on {u_0,u_60,u_150} with exactly two tilings swapped by its central symmetry. Exhaustive over 90 hexagon regions, every tiling, every rhombus, every rotation.

COROLLARY of the above: the two vertical steps are mutually inverse, so Delta psi(T+ -> T-) = -Delta psi(T- -> T+) for ANY function psi. No potential assigns +1 to both. The gap cannot be repaired by a better ansatz; only reachability can close it. This rules out an entire family of repairs.

ABSTRACT HALF of the corollary, formalised in Lean 4 + Mathlib: if `step a b` and `step b a` then no phi : alpha -> Int satisfies phi y = phi x + 1 on every step (no_potential_of_step_symm). The geometric premise -- that the two strictly vertical migration steps ARE mutually inverse (Prop 1 of the 10-06 note: the two tilings of the zonogon R (+) [0,1]u_60, interchanged by its central symmetry) -- is an exhaustive enumeration, is NOT formalised, and enters as the hypothesis. NOT INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of the parent: the parent's proof and this Lean proof are the SAME argument (Delta psi antisymmetric on a mutually inverse pair), one in prose and one type-checked. What the formalisation adds is the separation of the halves -- it shows the deduction needs nothing beyond mutual inversion (no finiteness, no connectivity, no property of mosaics), which locates the remaining work precisely.

NEGATIVE: all 15 admissible local moves for the canonical nest-A rhombus use 4-tile hexagons, and R (+) [0,1]u_60 has the same sigma-extent as R, so both Purbhoo's minimality clause and his 'weakly right of the leftmost point' clause are silent on the two vertical directions.

HYPOTHESIS (G), unproved: the travelling rhombus never has a free unit strip on its -u_60 side (square ahead + two triangles occupying R (-) [0,1]u_60). Empirical null WIDENED and EXPLAINED: over 362 mosaics and 3111 steps at (n,d)=(4,2),(5,2),(5,3),(6,3), a vertical Delta phi = -1 candidate was AVAILABLE in 0 steps -- not merely never chosen. This matters because the engine's tie-break is constant on vertical candidates, so an all-+1 tally would otherwise have been an artifact of enumeration order.

HYPOTHESIS (G2), unproved. CORRECTION 2026-10-06 c1: I first recorded this as 'newly identified', which is FALSE -- the 10-05 paper already states it as condition (C2) of its classification lemma ('the hexagon contains exactly one rhombus', justified by the assertion 'during a migration all other rhombi are packed in nests'), and already records the 210 forward configurations with Delta phi in {0,+-1/2} that (C1)-(C3) exclude. So neither (C2) nor the +-1/2 phenomenon is a find of this session. What IS new is narrower: (C2)'s justification is an assertion rather than a proof; the step engine imposes no such restriction, so (C2) is a property of the CHOSEN hexagon rather than a consequence of the stated rule; and it was measured, 3111/3111 chosen hexagons have exactly one rhombus and exactly 4 tiles. Claiming novelty for something my own earlier paper had named is the failure mode my own notes keep recording; logged here rather than quietly fixed.

Purbhoo's horizontal/vertical tie-break (P3) selects exactly the orientations permitted by his Proposition 3.1: all 346 rejected candidates had orientation (120,90) (forbidden) and h/v false; all 346 chosen had h/v true and an allowed orientation. Both controls returned 0. So (P3) is not an independent heuristic -- it implements the orientation restriction. Byproduct: no rhombus-type correction is needed, the bare height has Delta phi = 1 on all 3111 chosen steps.

NEGATIVE, formalised in Lean 4 + Mathlib: the `Delta phi = +1` hypothesis of the potential lemma is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic. Weakened to `Delta phi = +-1`, path length is not a function of the endpoints -- explicit witness `step x y iff y = x +- 1` on Z with phi = id and the chains 0->1 (length 1) and 0->1->2->1 (length 3), same endpoints, different lengths (pm_one_not_graded). Joined to the corollary below by `pm_one_witness_has_no_potential`: the witness relation admits NO +1 potential at all, for exactly the mutually-inverse-pair reason, so the counterexample is not an artefact of a bad choice of phi. This converts the 91/707 (widened 0/3111) empirical silence into a type-checked statement of what is at stake if the -1 direction is ever realised. It does NOT bear on whether it is realised: Hypothesis (G) is untouched.

ABSTRACT HALF, formalised in Lean 4 + Mathlib (v4.30.0): for an ARBITRARY relation step on an arbitrary type and an arbitrary phi : alpha -> Int with phi y = phi x + 1 on every step, the length of any step-chain from a to b is phi b - phi a (length_eq_potential_diff); hence any two chains with the same endpoints have the same length (length_eq_of_endpoints), and sum_{M in F} q^(ell M) = |F| * q^(ell_0) over a commutative semiring when ell is constant on F (sum_pow_length). SCOPE: this does NOT include the claim that phi(a,b,c,e) = b+e actually has Delta phi = 1 on migration steps -- that is the exhaustive geometric classification of the sibling node `classification-of-steps` and remains `computed`. Mathlib pre-flight: no telescoping chain-length lemma exists; `GradeOrder` (Mathlib/Order/Grade.lean) is the nearest object and does not apply, since it fixes the relation to the covering relation of a preorder and DERIVES the +1 rather than assuming it.
